minutes.headline: Board split 2-2 on the FY20 budget and old primary school articles, so no recommendation; Brooks House building sale recommended
minutes.summary: The board held a long public hearing on a draft special event permit policy, heard public comment on the town manager's review process, and put the Economic Development Committee on hold. It adopted a reimbursement policy and abated an old ambulance receivable. On Town Meeting articles, the board was deadlocked on the budget and the old primary school, and recommended only the Brooks House building sale.

what_happened.line: The Select Board split 2-2 on the FY20 budget article, so it made no recommendation to Town Meeting on the budget.
The board recommended approval of article 23, the Brooks House building sale; the outcome of the vote on the land conveyance, article 22, was not audible.
The board was also deadlocked on article 21, the old primary school, and made no recommendation on it.
The board adopted a reimbursement policy with edits and approved abating an old ambulance receivable that had no supporting records.
After a long hearing on a draft special event permit policy, the board agreed to a 48-hour cleanup period; no final adoption is recorded.

why_it_matters: Residents at Annual Town Meeting will vote on the FY20 budget and the old primary school without a Select Board recommendation, so the floor vote carries more weight.

The special event policy, which sets rules for overnight camping, event limits and cleanup, is still a draft, and residents raised concerns about how it relates to a citizen petition bylaw on the warrant.
watch_next: Select Board meeting April 16, and an abutters workshop the week of April 30; there is no meeting April 23.
An 8 a.m. Select Board meeting on the morning of Town Meeting, when the remaining articles (4, 5, 6, 8, 24, 33 and citizen petitions) were deferred to the floor.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on most routine votes (auto dealer license, hold on the Economic Development Committee, reimbursement policy, ambulance abatement, Article 23) and on the deferred articles. They differ on the FY20 budget vote, which ours records as "failed" and the official minutes record as a 2-2 tie with no position, and on the Article 22 and Article 23 votes and the Article 5 and 6 decisions.
